chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Jameela, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wrote to one of his companions, advising him:
I advise you, and myself, with the fear of God of the One to whom disobedience is not permissible, and from whom no other hope is sought, and from whom there is no self-sufficiency except by Him.
For indeed, whoever fears Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, becomes strong, satiated, quenched, and his intellect is elevated above the people of the world.
So his body is with the people of the world, but his heart and intellect are witnessing the Hereafter.
Thus, he extinguishes by the light of his heart whatever his eyes see of the love of the world.
So he considers its prohibitions as filthy and keeps away from its doubtful matters.

And he is content with the pure permissible, except what is inevitable for him: a crumb from it to strengthen his backbone, and a garment to cover his nakedness, from the coarsest and roughest of what he finds.
And there is no reliance or hope for him in what is inevitable for him from it.
So his reliance and hope fall upon the Creator of things.
So he strives, exerts himself, and exhausts his body until his ribs become visible and his eyes sink.
So Allah exchanges for him from that strength in his body and intensity in his intellect, and whatever is treasured for him in the Hereafter is greater.
Therefore, reject the world, for the love of the world blinds, deafens, mutes, and disgraces the necks.
So make up for what remains of your life and do not say 'Tomorrow' or 'After tomorrow'.
For indeed, those who were before you perished by their staying upon aspirations and procrastination.
Until the Command of Allah came to them suddenly while they were oblivious.
So they were carried on their planks into their dark, narrow graves.
And their children and family members had submitted them.
So turn to Allah with a penitent heart from rejecting the world, and with a determination in which there is no weakness nor exhaustion.
May Allah assist us and you in obeying Him, and may Allah grant us and you success in His pleasure.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on detachment from the world and focusing on the Hereafter?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s epistolary advice on *zuhd* (asceticism), emphasizing that true piety involves minimizing worldly needs to the bare essentials while maintaining a heart fully oriented toward the Hereafter. It underscores the practical discipline of enduring physical hardship in pursuit of spiritual strength, warning against the paralyzing effects of procrastination (*takhfir*) and the illusion of security in material wealth.
